lens.subject: Is one bundle per run the delivery rule now?
lens.message:
The memory you saved settles how reactions get delivered. You put it this way: "we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four." You also held the cutoff against Tina's pushback: the bundle closes when the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run. Per-skill delivery with client-side collapsing was considered and rejected because it moves the ordering problem onto the reader.

[The reaction delivery doc](docs/reaction-delivery.md) says the opposite today. Its opening reads: "Each reaction skill sends its own message to the person as soon as it finishes: the refraction, the question and the review each arrive on their own, in whatever order the skills complete. Readers collapse duplicates on their side." That is the alternative you rejected, written as current behavior. After this change it would rest on the bundle instead: one bundle per run per person, closed when the run closes, with no reader-side collapsing or ordering.

Is that the right way to read what you ruled: one bundle per run, closing with the run, and no collapsing on the reader's side? If I have it wrong, tell me how.

It reaches just this one doc — it is the only document in the repo that describes delivery, and everything in it moves.
